core.title: Bind every telemetry test to the item and the acceptance that requires it
core.given: A test file contains a real telemetry binding construct (a telemetry test; a real one is not inside a string literal) in a repository that has adopted the telemetry rule family
core.when: the test is validated or its bindings are written or changed, including unchanged tests re-judged after tracking-plan changes
core.then: Each telemetry binding must be a well-formed concrete URN resolving to a tracking-plan item, and the test must carry acceptance bindings naming acceptances declared in the plan, at least one of which has a telemetry decision that requires that item.
prefer: Bind both ends of the proof: the test's own identifier, the acceptance it covers, and the telemetry item it exercises.
In a test covering many acceptances, ensure at least one bound acceptance's decision lists the item.
avoid: Binding an item with no acceptance — it proves something nobody required.
Binding an acceptance whose decision does not list the item — a test proves a requirement, not an acquaintance.
Non-concrete or unresolvable telemetry bindings; acceptance bindings absent from the plan.
unless: A test counts as a telemetry test only by a telemetry kind segment in its own identifier (the segments the profile supplies, urn.test_kinds#telemetry) or by the telemetry-test colocation name pattern the profile supplies (suffix.telemetry_test), with no telemetry binding construct: the captured-sink and identity rules judge it instead.
The repository has not adopted this rule family (inert until adoption, like every rule in it).
core.why: This is the covers edge of the telemetry graph (acceptance → item → test); without both bindings a test proves nothing required or a relationship the plan never declared.
evidence: The telemetry-test check reports no finding for any telemetry binding in the test file.
For each binding: the URN parses, resolves in the tracking-plan registry, acceptance bindings are present and exist in the plan, and at least one bound acceptance's telemetry decision lists the item.
verification: Scope: a telemetry test is a test file with a telemetry binding construct, a telemetry kind segment in its own identifier (urn.test_kinds#telemetry), or a name matching the telemetry-test colocation pattern (suffix.telemetry_test); this check judges only test files that contain a real telemetry binding construct — the others are out of its scope and are judged by the captured-sink and identity rules.
A bound acceptance is the acceptance named by the test's acceptance binding; its telemetry decision must list the bound item — a test proves a requirement, not an acquaintance.

Every telemetry binding is judged on its own line, in order: concrete-URN grammar, registry resolution, presence of acceptance bindings, the bindings' existence in the plan, and at least one bound acceptance's decision actually requiring the bound item.
A test may legitimately cover many acceptances (the two-level covers model); the requiring one may be any of them, so the judgement runs over the whole bound set — none requiring is the finding.
A binding construct that appears only inside a string literal is not a binding — ignore it.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: a real telemetry binding construct present in a test file (not inside a string literal), whether or not the test was edited

fires: A test file contains a telemetry binding whose URN is malformed or does not resolve to a tracking-plan item.
A test file has a telemetry binding but no acceptance binding.
A test's acceptance binding names an acceptance not declared in the plan.
A test binds a telemetry item and one or more acceptances, but none of the bound acceptances' telemetry decisions lists that item.
An unchanged test's existing telemetry binding becomes invalid after the tracking plan changes (item removed, acceptance removed, or decision no longer lists the item) and is found during validation.
doesNotFire: A test is a telemetry test only by a telemetry kind segment in its own identifier (urn.test_kinds#telemetry) or by the telemetry-test colocation name pattern (suffix.telemetry_test), with no telemetry binding construct (the captured-sink and identity rules judge it).
The telemetry binding syntax appears only inside a string literal.
A test binds many acceptances and at least one of them requires the bound item.
The repository has not adopted the telemetry rule family.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that count as test files for this rule: the neutral activation fact file_kind 'test' must resolve to them; the check scans unit-test files for telemetry bindings.
Spec (acceptance-test) files count as test files too: a spec may legitimately cover many acceptances, and the judgement runs over the whole bound set.

The kind segments of a test's own identifier that mark it as a telemetry test; the core's exception, scope statement and doesNotFire case reference them: a test identified only this way, with no telemetry binding construct, is out of this rule's scope and is judged by the captured-sink and identity rules instead.

The file-name pattern by which a colocated test file is identified as a telemetry test — a family-scoped subset of test files, not a file kind; the core's exception, scope statement and doesNotFire case reference it: a file matching this pattern with no telemetry binding construct is out of this rule's scope and is judged by the captured-sink and identity rules instead.
The syntax by which a test file binds itself to a telemetry item — the construct this rule judges (a real one is not inside a string literal).
The URN shape of a tracking-plan telemetry item; each telemetry binding must match it with concrete (non-generic) identifiers and resolve to an item in the plan's registry.
The syntax by which a test binds itself to the acceptances it covers; the rule requires these bindings to be present and to name acceptances declared in the plan.
The acceptance URN grammar; a bound acceptance must be declared in the plan under this shape.

neutralityNotes: The core speaks of a 'telemetry binding construct' and 'acceptance binding'; their concrete syntaxes come from the profile keys urn.binding.telemetry and urn.binding.acceptance (the telemetry keys are proposed, since the closed vocabulary has no telemetry artifact kind). Both headerless telemetry-test identification modes are profile data under proposed keys: the identifier kind segments (urn.test_kinds#telemetry; Bun: TELEMETRY/EVENT/METRIC) and the colocation name pattern (suffix.telemetry_test; Bun: *.telemetry.test.*). They are referenced by the core's exception, scope statement and doesNotFire case, so the exception is neither dropped nor narrowed. How URNs resolve against the tracking-plan registry is left to each realization's checker; the Bun validator and finding ids are bunOnly. Per-rule severity and strict disposition stay in core.verification per the notProfileKeys rule. Nothing else resisted neutralization.
